title: Standard 4.2: Ionic Compound Formulas
format: Matches Kai's Quiz 9 structure: Q4, Q5, Q6 (table), Q7 (naming table)

4.2.1.description: Assess whether ionic formula is neutral

4.2.2.description: Determine number of atoms in compound

4.2.3.description: Use preferred charge to write formulas

4.2.5.description: Predict charge of single ions from formula

Q4.prompt: Two compounds with polyatomic ions. Only one has the proper formula. Identify the polyatomic ion in each and explain why each formula is or is not correct.

compounds.explanation: Mg is +2, each OH is -1. Three OH gives -3. Total: +2 + (-3) = -1. NOT neutral. Correct formula is Mg(OH)2.
Each K is +1, two K gives +2. SO4 is -2. Total: +2 + (-2) = 0. Neutral. This is the correct formula.

charges.gradingNote: NO3 is nitrate = 1- (not 2-). This is where Kai made his error on the real quiz with Fe(NO3)2.

atomCount.gradingNote: 1 Ca, 2 N (1 x 2), 6 O (3 x 2). The subscript 2 outside the parentheses multiplies both N and O.

rows.gradingNote: Polyatomic ion (hydroxide). 1:1 ratio. No parentheses needed.
Both 2:2 charge. 1:1 ratio. Copper charge given as 2+ (student should be able to use this to predict).

formulaToName.gradingNote: Type I: K is always +1, no Roman numeral. O root + -ide = oxide.
Type I: Mg is always +2, no Roman numeral. Br root + -ide = bromide.
Type II: Fe is a transition metal. 2 Cl- = -2, so Fe = +2. MUST include (II). Common error: forgetting the Roman numeral.
Type III: Ca is always +2 (no Roman numeral). OH = hydroxide (polyatomic ion name, not -ide suffix).
Type III: Both ions are polyatomic. NH4 = ammonium, PO4 = phosphate. No metal, no Roman numeral.

nameToFormula.name: Potassium nitrate
nameToFormula.gradingNote: K+ and NO3-. 1:1 ratio. No parentheses (only one nitrate).

nameToFormula.name: Copper(II) sulfate
nameToFormula.gradingNote: Cu2+ (Roman numeral II tells you) and SO4 2-. 1:1 ratio.

nameToFormula.name: Aluminum chloride
nameToFormula.gradingNote: Al3+ and Cl-. Need 3 Cl- to balance.

nameToFormula.name: Barium phosphate
nameToFormula.gradingNote: Ba2+ and PO4 3-. Cross charges: 3 Ba, 2 PO4. Parentheses around PO4.
